--- title: "Reworked Visualization" subtitle: "this graph sucks lol" author: "Taj Mckinnon" date: "2026-11-18" categories: [code, analysis] image: "image.jpg" echo: false message: false warning: false --- I present to you all: a visualization I made on the 2nd day of class. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: Hurts your eyes, doesn't it? To be fair, I was relearning R at this point, and it had been a year since I had used it (oops...) so...
Let's see how I can make this look better! Maybe a new splash of color...? ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: Well that certainly isn't confusing at all. Let's try a different graph style this time, along with a new color palette. (i'm rereading this and i'm realizing that i sound like an LLM, which makes me sad. although, does that mean i'm losing my humanity, or is an LLM getting better at mimicking it? questions for later i guess.) ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: Now that's more like it!
The color palette is all nice, the graph doesn't look like a heart rate monitor, and it still gets the message across! It's all I ever wanted! For the previous one, I was too focused on including the spikes in the graph. The preservationist in me wanted to keep everything on the graph, which isn't a bad mentality to have at all! Just not a good mentality for data sometimes, since then you can end up with the rainbow mess that was the first graph. Hopefully my future graphs will be better...
